data.title: Create a controlled wet-ground variant
data.summary: A dry pavement material and a separate puddle mask. An LLM-assisted recipe with a concrete practice case, visual procedure and review gates.

facts.text: Principled BSDF combines surface layers with configurable material parameters.

prerequisites: An authorized Blender shaders / runtime materials environment and a recorded tool version. Blender-specific references here are pinned to the 4.5 manual; check differences in your installed version.
Practice inputs: A dry pavement material and a separate puddle mask.

Permission to use the source assets and a writable derived-output location. Use a disposable project copy for edits. An MCP connection is optional; reviewed scripts or manual tool actions can follow the same procedure.
steps: Inspect the existing project, asset registry and target runtime for an equivalent wet ground workflow. Reuse the closest source and preserve its original files.

Give Claude Code, Codex or another authorized coding assistant this practice brief: A dry pavement material and a separate puddle mask. Ask for a small plan and parameter/script diff; verify names and APIs against the installed tool version before applying it.
Reuse the dry material and drive roughness changes from the puddle mask
Keep raised dry areas visible; add geometry only for puddle edges that affect silhouette
Compare dry and wet presets under identical lighting and export the intended fallback

Save the derived candidate separately, record software versions and source/output identities, then perform the acceptance checks. Keep unresolved quality, performance and rights questions in the receipt.
data.output: A versioned create a controlled wet-ground variant candidate, the input/parameter table, source identity and a review receipt with the checks below.
validation: The puddle mask does not invert at UV seams
The wet preset retains readable pavement detail
Record actual observations separately from expected results; missing tests remain unrun.
limitations: This is an artistic wetness effect, not a measured water-film simulation.
Sintra-authored proposal, not an executed Blender/engine/solver test. The diagram illustrates the procedure and is not a render or execution receipt.
Cloud chat cannot directly control a local 3D app without an appropriate authorized bridge. Tool access, model availability, paid services and rendering resources must be checked separately.
tips: Avoid painting directional reflections into reusable base color.
Let the LLM draft and explain bounded changes; use deterministic software to measure geometry, calculate trajectories and validate files.

data.prompt: Help me create a controlled wet-ground variant in [existing authorized project]. First find an equivalent asset/workflow and inspect the installed tool version. Practice brief: A dry pavement material and a separate puddle mask. Propose the smallest parameter or script diff and explain each tool action. Follow the linked procedure, preserve original assets and stop on missing inputs or unsupported APIs. Check: The puddle mask does not invert at UV seams; The wet preset retains readable pavement detail. Return actual observations, source/output identities and blockers. Do not call expected results completed tests or publish private source paths.
